exposure: Cesarean section delivery (as the event initiating costs)
outcome: Patient-level out-of-pocket costs up to 30 days postoperative
Main contributors to c-section follow-up costs
cohort: Women who delivered via cesarean section at Kirehe District Hospital in rural Rwanda between September 2019 and February 2020.
finding: Costs associated with surgical follow-up significantly contribute to the risk of catastrophic health expenditures (CHE) in rural Rwanda, increasing the CHE rate from 27% (considering only in-hospital costs) to 77% (including post-discharge expenses) up to 30 days postoperative.
